<reason>B won a close, high-quality debate by locking onto the motion as written: not any reporter versus a vacuum, but whether firewalled public pay would net-reduce polarization and corruption. A’s news-desert case was vivid and current, yet never fully converted into evidence for this instrument; B repeatedly treated that gap as fatal and kept independence as the condition the promised reductions require. A’s “unfalsifiable capture proves too much” close landed, but B’s funder-identity and “credential as cover” frames stayed live and easier to vote on.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B2.1–B2.4: journalism is not an IG/judge, and desert studies measure dying private papers, not a subsidy—this defined the clash.</best_rebuttal>
